title: Using LIFO (Stack) for Connection Allocation under Light Load
pattern: Implementing a resource pool (such as connection pools or thread pools) that relies on a Last-In-First-Out (LIFO/Stack) allocation strategy for dispensing handles.
why_bad: Under light load, only the single connection at the top of the stack gets repeatedly checked out, used, and checked back in [196]. The remaining pooled connections sit idle [196]. If their idle time exceeds stateful network devices' (firewalls) inactivity timeouts, the firewall silently evicts them [196]. When load eventually spikes, checkouts of these idle connections immediately hang as threads attempt to write/read to evicted sockets [196, 197].
detection: Identify pool implementations that return connection resources from the top/tail of a stack structure (like `.pop()`) rather than from a FIFO queue.
fix: Use a First-In-First-Out (FIFO) queue for pooling resources to ensure even, periodic utilization of all pooled connections [196].
source: Michael T. Nygard, *Release It!*, Chapter 2 (Resource Pools) / passages [196, 197].
